skill.name: chronicle-session-documenter
skill.description: Document Chronicle development sessions as structured Obsidian notes. Use MCP tools when available or Chronicle CLI output when MCP is not available.
skill.summary: Create structured Obsidian notes from Chronicle development sessions.
skill.author: ChandlerHardy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, MCP tool names, and scoped Chronicle CLI examples. One confirmed issue remains: the CLI workflow writes session details to a predictable /tmp file, which can expose private development metadata. The skill also has a medium-confidence integrity risk because its main write example uses overwrite mode before the later note-existence warning.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary file for session export
remediation.suggestion: Avoid writing Chronicle output to /tmp/session_10.txt. Capture command output directly or use a private temporary file with restricted permissions.
Require a read_note check and explicit user confirmation before using overwrite mode for an existing session note.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Note Overwrite Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The MCP example writes a session note with overwrite mode, while later guidance says to check existing notes first. An agent following the example could replace manually edited Obsidian notes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The overwrite setting is explicit in the example, and the later warning confirms existing notes are a known concern. Risk depends on whether the agent checks before writing.

content.value_statement: Development sessions are hard to review when details stay in chat history or local logs. This skill turns Chronicle data into structured Obsidian notes with summaries, metadata, and links.
actual_capabilities: Queries Chronicle session summaries through MCP when available.
Uses Chronicle CLI output as a portable fallback workflow.
Creates Obsidian session notes with metadata and Markdown sections.
Adds wikilinks for sessions, repositories, and related commits.
Supports single-session, daily-session, and topic-based documentation workflows.
limitations: Requires Chronicle data and either MCP tools or the Chronicle CLI.
Recent sessions may not have summaries ready immediately.
CLI output must be parsed from formatted text.
Sensitive session details should be reviewed before writing to synced vaults.

use_cases.title: Create a Daily Development Journal
use_cases.description: Turn completed Chronicle sessions into organized Obsidian notes after each workday.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Handoffs
use_cases.description: Summarize accomplishments, decisions, changed files, and blockers for team review.

use_cases.title: Build a Searchable Knowledge Base
use_cases.description: Link related sessions, commits, repositories, and topics across a long-running project.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Document Chronicle session 10 to my Obsidian vault.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for one known session ID.

prompt_templates.title: Document Today
prompt_templates.prompt: Find today's completed Chronicle sessions and create Obsidian notes for them. Ask before overwriting existing notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Daily documentation after a development session block.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Decisions and Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian note for session 24. Include accomplishments, key decisions, changed files, blockers, and related commits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed documentation for a session with technical decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Document Topic History
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Chronicle for sessions about authentication from the last week. Document the three most relevant sessions with wikilinks between related notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced research workflow across multiple sessions.

output_examples.input: Document session 10 to my Obsidian vault.
output_examples.output: Creates a Session 10 note with metadata, summary, accomplishments, decisions, files, blockers, and related links.
Produces separate session notes for the day and links them to repositories, commits, and previous sessions.

output_examples.input: Find sessions about authentication and document the important ones.
output_examples.output: Searches Chronicle, selects relevant sessions, and writes linked notes focused on the authentication work.

best_practices: Ask before overwriting any existing Obsidian note.
Review generated summaries for secrets before syncing notes.
Prefer MCP data when available because it is structured.
anti_patterns: Do not store session exports in predictable temporary files.
Do not document active sessions before summaries are ready.
Do not write private project details to a shared vault without review.

faq.question: Does this skill require MCP tools?
faq.answer: No. It prefers MCP tools, but it can use Chronicle CLI output when MCP is not available.

faq.question: What does the Obsidian note include?
faq.answer: The note can include metadata, a summary, accomplishments, decisions, changed files, blockers, and related links.

faq.question: Can it document multiple sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for today's sessions, topic searches, and batch session summaries.

faq.question: Will it overwrite existing notes?
faq.answer: It should check for existing notes first and ask before replacing manually edited content.

faq.question: Does it send data to an external service?
faq.answer: No external network service is described. Data moves from Chronicle into the user's Obsidian vault.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing notes?
faq.answer: Users should review summaries, repository paths, file names, blockers, and synced vault settings for sensitive information.
